overview: This resolution, passed by both the House and the Senate, lets Emancipation Hall, the large main hall of the Capitol Visitor Center in Washington, be used on April 14, 2026, for a ceremony marking the Days of Remembrance of victims of the Holocaust. It says the physical setup for the event must follow whatever conditions the Architect of the Capitol, the office that runs the Capitol buildings and grounds, sets. Congress needs to approve this kind of special use of the space, and this resolution gives that approval for one day. Congress gave final approval on March 2, 2026.
for: Supporters say holding the Holocaust remembrance ceremony in the Capitol gives the memory of the victims a place of honor and reminds the public and lawmakers of the lessons of that history.
against: Critics say the resolution is a routine, symbolic step that only books a room for one event and does not change any law or spending.
